allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each fixed integer n at least 2, consider all sign sequences of length n minus 1 with entries plus or minus 1. Define f(s) as the number of permutations of {1, 2, ..., n} whose consecutive differences have the prescribed signs. The task is to identify exactly which sign sequences s maximize f(s).
allowed_dependency_manifest.label: root_semantic_sketch

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

payload.role_in_assembly: Identifies the total weight of each full parity class with the count of an alternating sign sequence of length n-1.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Define E_r for each positive integer r as the number of permutations of {1,...,r} whose entries alternate up and down, starting with an increase at the first step, and set E_0 to 1. For each integer n at least 2, define w_j as the binomial coefficient n minus 1 choose j minus 1 times E_{j-1} times E_{n-j}. Then, for that n, the sum of w_j over odd j from 1 to n equals E_n, and the sum of w_j over even j from 1 to n also equals E_n.
quantifier_order: For each integer r at least 1, define E_r by counting permutations b_1 through b_r of {1,...,r} satisfying the alternating sign inequalities, and also set E_0 equal to 1.
For the fixed integer n at least 2, define w_j for each j from 1 to n.
For that same fixed n, the sum of w_j over odd j equals E_n.
For that same fixed n, the sum of w_j over even j equals E_n.

payload.statement_nl: For each integer r >= 1, let E_r be the number of permutations (b_1,...,b_r) of {1,...,r} such that (-1)^(i-1) * (b_{i+1} - b_i) > 0 for every 1 <= i <= r-1, and set E_0 = 1. Fix an integer n >= 2 and define w_j = binom(n-1, j-1) * E_{j-1} * E_{n-j} for 1 <= j <= n. Then sum over odd j in {1,...,n} of w_j is equal to E_n, and sum over even j in {1,...,n} of w_j is also equal to E_n.

result_payload.proof_nl:
For m >= 1, let U_m be the set of permutations c = (c_1,...,c_m) of {1,...,m} such that (-1)^(i-1)(c_{i+1}-c_i) > 0 for every 1 <= i <= m-1; thus |U_m| = E_m. Also let U_0 consist of the empty permutation, so |U_0| = E_0 = 1.

For m >= 1, let V_m be the set of permutations c = (c_1,...,c_m) of {1,...,m} such that (-1)^i(c_{i+1}-c_i) > 0 for every 1 <= i <= m-1; this is the alternating pattern starting with a decrease. Let V_0 also consist of the empty permutation.

The map c = (c_1,...,c_m) -> (m+1-c_1,...,m+1-c_m) is a bijection V_m -> U_m, because for each i,
(-1)^(i-1)((m+1-c_{i+1})-(m+1-c_i)) = -(-1)^(i-1)(c_{i+1}-c_i) = (-1)^i(c_{i+1}-c_i) > 0.
Hence |V_m| = |U_m| = E_m for all m >= 0.

We also use the following simple relabeling fact. If S = {s_1 < ... < s_m} is any m-element set, then the map
(u_1,...,u_m) -> (s_{u_1},...,s_{u_m})
is a bijection from U_m onto the permutations of S satisfying the U-pattern, and from V_m onto the permutations of S satisfying the V-pattern, because s_a < s_b iff a < b. So the number of permutations of an m-element set with either pattern depends only on m.

Now fix n >= 2 and let A = U_n. Then |A| = E_n.

First, count A by the position of the maximum element n. If b = (b_1,...,b_n) is in A and b_j = n, then j must be even. Indeed, if j = 1 then b_1 < b_2, so b_1 is not the maximum. If j > 1 is odd, then j-1 is even, and the defining inequality at i = j-1 gives b_j < b_{j-1}, again impossible for the maximum. Thus the sets
A_j = { b in A : b_j = n }
for even j form a disjoint partition of A.

Fix an even j. We count A_j. For b in A_j, let L = {b_1,...,b_{j-1}} and R = {b_{j+1},...,b_n}. Then L is any subset of {1,...,n-1} of size j-1, so there are binom(n-1,j-1) choices for L.

The left block (b_1,...,b_{j-1}) satisfies the U-pattern on the set L, since it obeys the original inequalities for indices 1,...,j-2. Therefore, by the relabeling fact, there are E_{j-1} possibilities for the left block.

For the right block, write c_t = b_{j+t} for 1 <= t <= n-j. For 1 <= t <= n-j-1, the original inequality at i = j+t gives
(-1)^(j+t-1)(c_{t+1}-c_t) > 0.
Because j is even, (-1)^(j+t-1) = (-1)^(t-1), so the right block also satisfies the U-pattern. Hence there are E_{n-j} possibilities for the right block.

Conversely, given any subset L of {1,...,n-1} of size j-1, any U-pattern permutation of L, and any U-pattern permutation of R = {1,...,n-1} \ L, inserting n between those two blocks produces an element of A_j. The inequalities inside each block hold by construction, and the boundary inequalities at position j are automatic because n is larger than every element of L and R; when one side is empty, there is simply no boundary inequality on that side. This reconstruction is unique. Therefore
|A_j| = binom(n-1,j-1) E_{j-1} E_{n-j} = w_j.

Since the A_j for even j partition A, we get
E_n = |A| = sum over even j of |A_j| = sum over even j of w_j.

Now count the same set A by the position of the minimum element 1. If b = (b_1,...,b_n) is in A and b_j = 1, then j must be odd. Indeed, if j is even, then j-1 is odd, and the defining inequality at i = j-1 gives b_j > b_{j-1}, impossible for the minimum. Thus the sets
B_j = { b in A : b_j = 1 }
for odd j form a disjoint partition of A.

Fix an odd j. We count B_j. For b in B_j, let L = {b_1,...,b_{j-1}} and R = {b_{j+1},...,b_n}. Then L is any subset of {2,...,n} of size j-1, so there are again binom(n-1,j-1) choices for L.

As before, the left block (b_1,...,b_{j-1}) satisfies the U-pattern, so there are E_{j-1} possibilities for it.

For the right block, again write c_t = b_{j+t} for 1 <= t <= n-j. For 1 <= t <= n-j-1, the original inequality at i = j+t gives
(-1)^(j+t-1)(c_{t+1}-c_t) > 0.
Because j is odd, (-1)^(j+t-1) = (-1)^t, so the right block satisfies the V-pattern. Hence there are |V_{n-j}| = E_{n-j} possibilities for the right block.

Conversely, given any subset L of {2,...,n} of size j-1, any U-pattern permutation of L, and any V-pattern permutation of R = {2,...,n} \ L, inserting 1 between those two blocks produces an element of B_j. The inequalities inside each block hold by construction, and the boundary inequalities at position j are automatic because 1 is smaller than every element of L and R. Again the reconstruction is unique. Therefore
|B_j| = binom(n-1,j-1) E_{j-1} E_{n-j} = w_j.

Since the B_j for odd j partition A, we get
E_n = |A| = sum over odd j of |B_j| = sum over odd j of w_j.

Thus both parity-restricted sums are equal to E_n, exactly as claimed.
result_payload.proof_summary: Count alternating permutations of {1,...,n} in two different ways. Partition by the position of the maximum n: it can occur only at even positions, and for fixed even j the permutation is determined by choosing the j-1 values to the left of n and then choosing independent alternating permutations on the left and right blocks, giving w_j. This proves the even-j sum is E_n. Partition instead by the position of the minimum 1: it can occur only at odd positions, and for fixed odd j the left block is alternating while the right block is alternating starting with a decrease; complementing values gives the same count E_{n-j} for the latter. This gives the odd-j sum as E_n.
